sections.title: Giving Directions
sections.content: Directions are instructions, so they use the imperative you met in Lesson 9 — the él/ella form, aimed at one person. That is why they all look like ordinary present-tense verbs: camina, gira, cruza, pasa, sigue. Only 'seguir' bends, changing its e to i: sigue.

items.spanish: Camina todo recto hasta el semáforo.
items.english: Walk straight on as far as the traffic lights.

items.spanish: Después gira a la derecha y sigue dos calles.
items.english: Then turn right and carry on for two streets.

items.spanish: Pasa el parque y cruza la calle.
items.english: Go past the park and cross the street.

items.spanish: No encuentro la cafetería. Te llamo por teléfono.
items.english: I can't find the café. I'll call you.

sections.content: Strung together, directions need no linking words at all: 'camina todo recto, gira a la derecha, cruza la calle'. Spanish gives them one after another, exactly as a recipe gives its steps.
